newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM urges Khmer Rouge leaders to defect.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM urges Khmer Rouge leaders to defect.

text.p: Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Thursday called on two top leaders of the Khmer Rouge guerrilla faction still allied with hardliner Pol Pot to join the Phnom Penh government.
He said the defection of the nominal leader of the Khmer Rouge, Khieu Samphan, and the group's defence chief, Son Sen, was needed to bring peace to Cambodia.
"Please come to join the government for the national reconciliation to finish the war completely," he said in a television broadcast.

Ranariddh's appeal follows the first direct talks, held in Thailand on Thursday, between Cambodia's co-defence ministers and Ieng Sary, leader of the dissident Khmer Rouge faction that broke from Pol Pot last month.

"Now we have Ieng Sary, (disident divisional commanders) Sok Peap, Ei Chien. The war is not completely finished as we must fight with Khieu Samphan, Son Sen, (hardline northern forces commander) Ta Mok and others," Ranariddh said.

Khieu Samphan and Son Sen were signed the 1991 Cambodian peace accord on behalf of the Khmer Rouge and represented the group on the interim 1991-93 sovereignty body, the Supreme National Council (SNC).
Ranariddh noted that Khieu Samphan had always shown respect towards Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk, the main advocate of reconciliation.

In 1979, Ieng Sary and Pol Pot were sentenced to death in absentia for their role in the Khmer Rouge reign of terror known as the "killing fields." More than one million people died of disease, starvation or overwork in mass labour camps.
As Pol Pot's defence ministers, Khieu Samphan and Son Sen were regarded as architects of the genocide.
Khieu Samphan was driven out of Phnom Penh by an irate mob when he arrived for his first SNC meeting in November 1991.
Son Sen and Khieu Samphan later returned to the capital and set up an office next to the royal palace. The office closed shortly before parliament outlawed the Khmer Rouge in July 1994.

Khieu Samphan has been heard on Khmer Rouge radio in recent weeks denouncing Ieng Sary and his supporters as traitors. Thai intelligence reports have suggested he is a virtual prisoner of the hardliners and was being forced to repeat their line.

The SNC was composed of the four parties that signed the 1991 peace accords. Its mandate expired when Cambodia adopted a constitutional monarchy, rejected by the Khmer Rouge, in September 1993. The guerrillas have been fighting the government ever since.
